issues.description: The problem statement uses the method name getFeedingSound() in several places (for expected return values in Part 2 and in the song template), while the UML, template code comments, and the solution implementation consistently use messageOnFeed() as the abstract feeding-sound method on Animal. This name mismatch between the textual specification and the class/interface design is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which method to implement or call when producing feeding sounds.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the problem statement text (and the song example) to refer to messageOnFeed() instead of getFeedingSound(). Alternatively, if getFeedingSound() is the intended name, update the UML, template, and solution to use getFeedingSound() (or provide a small adapter method delegating between the two) so all references match.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to a feeding-sound method named getFeedingSound(), while the UML, template expectations, and the reference solution use the method name messageOnFeed(). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (the animal's feeding sound) can confuse students about which method to implement and which method feedAllAnimals() should call.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Update the problem statement occurrences of getFeedingSound() to messageOnFeed() (or, alternatively, rename messageOnFeed() in template/solution to getFeedingSound()), so that the method name is consistent with the UML and reference implementation and students clearly know which method to implement and call.
